items.title: Six Races Lineup: Twelve Travellers at True Height
items.caption: Left to right, a man then a woman of each race: Maro Folk, Ondo Forge, Linde Folk, Daro Guard, Tava Kin, Silme Seers. Relative heights for the 3D prototype; designs are preferred prototypes, not locked canon. Ondo Forge redrawn taller at the owner's request.
items.prompt: Wide landscape image, 16:9, plain off-white paper background with one thin pale grey ground line across the bottom 8 percent of the frame. Twelve full body adult characters stand in one single row on that ground line, all facing the camera, arms relaxed, evenly spaced, with no gaps wider than one figure. The row is six pairs, a man then a woman in each pair, from left to right: pair one is the version 2 human pair from this conversation, blue, cream and gold adventurer outfits, friendly faces, the woman with long hair and a lightly fitted outfit that shows little skin; pair two is the short and sturdy pair with the short beard version B man from this conversation, young faces, red hair, work goggles on the forehead; pair three is the slim pointed-ear pair from this conversation; pair four is the large broad-shouldered pair from this conversation; pair five is the dog-eared beastfolk pair from this conversation with the exact ear design already chosen; pair six is the pale-haired pair from this conversation. Heights as a share of the frame height, measured from the ground line to the top of the head: pair four man 85 percent, woman 78 percent; pairs one, three and six men 68 percent, women 63 percent; pair five man 62 percent, woman 58 percent, ears not counted; pair two man 46 percent, woman 43 percent. Keep each design exactly as last shown in this conversation, same faces, hair, colours and outfits, nothing redrawn from scratch. A soft grey shadow under every figure. Anime character design sheet, hand-painted digital illustration with fine dark outlines, soft cel shading, sharp line highlights and visible fabric texture. Clear colours with warm accents. No text, no letters, no labels, no numbers, no height ruler, no logo, no watermark. Owner edit in the chat afterwards: the short sturdy pair was too small, so pair two was redrawn taller, measured about 49 and 45 percent of the frame height, 81 percent of the pair one man.
